titleEn: A Little Prick, a Strong Dingding!

pages.text: "Cough, cough!" Dingding sat on the floor, coughing. Their forehead was hot and their nose was stuffy. "Mom, I don't want to go to the paddy today."
Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, touched Dingding's forehead. "The doctor is visiting the village below. Let's go." "I don't want a shot! I'll just sleep and get better!"
A white cloth covered a spot in Mr. Ming's yard. Dingding pulled their bamboo hat down to their nose and hid behind Mom. Mom laughed. "I can see your feet below that hat!"
The goat doctor, who sometimes visited the lower village, sat in front of Dingding. "Did you know there are little workers inside your tummy?" "Workers...?" Dingding lifted the hat a little.
"They keep you strong," the doctor whispered. "But cold bugs have come in, and the workers are tired. That's why your forehead is so hot."
"This shot gives those tired workers a little meal. Then they jump up and chase the cold bugs away!" The doctor sang, "A Little Prick, a Strong Dingding!"
Dingding breathed out and held out an arm. Their eyes closed tight. Prick! It was already over. "Oh! That didn't hurt at all! A Little Prick, a Strong Dingding!"
Dingding sniffed the sunny smell of the yard. With the bamboo hat off, Dingding lifted their chin high. Not a tear! The doctor held up a finger.

On the way home, Dingding explained happily. "One, take a big breath! Two, hold out my arm! Three, call the workers in my tummy!" At home, Dingding swallowed the medicine and drank water. After a nap, their forehead felt cool.

Mom hugged Dingding and put her cheek against their forehead. "Your fever is gone!" When you are sick, seeing the doctor helps you get better quickly. Dingding brushed off their apron. "A Little Prick, a Strong Dingding!"
